issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Pneumatic.openValve: the UML/problem statement declares openValve() with no parameters (problem_statement.md line 18), while the solution's Pneumatic interface declares openValve(int duration) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java line 7). The solution's implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement a no-argument openValve() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/LaunchedDropdownTower.java line 15 and solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/LaunchedRollerCoaster.java line 15). This cross-artifact inconsistency will cause compilation failures in the provided solution and will confuse students about which signature they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the openValve signature consistent across all artifacts. Option A (recommended to match the UML/problem text): change the solution's Pneumatic interface to declare void openValve() and update/remove any duration parameter, ensuring implementing classes keep the no-arg signature. Option B: if a duration parameter is intended, update the UML and problem statement to declare openValve(int duration), and update the template and all implementing classes to implement that signature. Ensure the template Pneumatic.java and the exercise instructions reflect the chosen signature so students are not confused.
